findings.claim: Official application guidance separates bachelor entry qualifications from master’s prior-degree/recognition requirements and states that additional criteria vary by university and programme. Being an Indian college student is not itself a sufficient eligibility profile.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: High for the documented process; no segment-size estimate inferred

sources.title: Bachelor & Staatsexamen: entrance qualifications and course-specific criteria
Master: related prior degree, recognition and course-specific criteria

findings.implication: Segment the learning cohort by intended study level and actual qualification route. Keep both levels in product scope while asking different follow-up questions, instead of reusing a master-only questionnaire for everyone.

findings.claim: India-specific uni-assist notes request educational records and grading-system details. APS’s October 2026 notice makes the emerging dMAT procedure applicant-group and intake dependent, with transitions and an affected-field list still awaiting announcement; it is not a universal bachelor/master rule.
findings.label: Data
findings.sourceDate: APS updated 2026-10-15; uni-assist live page accessed 2026-10-25
findings.confidence: High for the published distinctions; the unresolved field mapping remains unknown

sources.title: Digital Master Test: staged applicant groups and transitional rules

findings.implication: Record current qualification, intended degree, intake and what is known versus missing. A participant with no test score can still be interviewed or shown orientation; a specific eligibility conclusion must preserve unresolved rules rather than auto-reject or assume compliance.

findings.claim: A useful initial audience model is a two-by-two grid: bachelor versus master intent, crossed with open exploration versus an existing shortlist. This is a synthesis of the founder’s two starting states and the official distinction between degree routes, not an observed prevalence or validated persona taxonomy.
findings.label: Assumption
findings.sourceDate: Founder brief 2026-10-25 plus current official process references
findings.confidence: Medium as a research design; Low as an empirical description of the market

sources.title: Bachelor & Staatsexamen: entrance qualifications and course-specific criteria

findings.implication: Recruit across all four cells to discover whether their jobs and evidence needs actually differ. Do not attach fictional names, ages, salaries, budgets, family classes or representative quotes to the segments.

findings.claim: Two publisher-run 2026 India studies describe students as active decision-makers while retaining family influence. Oxford International reports two datasets totalling 20,341 respondents, with item-specific questions; Acumen’s pulse explicitly is not nationally representative. These are broader education populations, not a Germany-app buyer panel.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: Medium for directional context; Low for any India-to-Germany subgroup or payer estimate

sources.title: Learning, independence and opportunity: what Indian students want from overseas education
10K Voices: International Education, Made in India — 2026 report

findings.implication: Treat the student as the user and ask who else participates in funding, risk and decisions. A parent may be an influencer or future payer, but do not assume control of an adult student’s account, disclose their profile automatically, or infer app willingness to pay from education funding.

findings.claim: DAAD India provides free information sessions, individual guidance and a peer ambassador network, and promotes personalized My GUIDE programme discovery. Acumen’s broader student pulse describes digital information and personal advice operating together; it does not establish one dominant channel for this Germany-first audience.
findings.label: Data
findings.sourceDate: DAAD live pages accessed 2026-10-25; Acumen report 2026-08
findings.confidence: High for the visible official alternatives; Medium for the broader behavior interpretation

findings.implication: Interview students about the official sites, AI, peers and advisers they actually used and what each failed to resolve. Campus/alumni contacts and relevant public communities are recruitment candidates, not proven density, approved distribution partnerships or cheap CAC.

findings.claim: The proposed audience criteria should use the student’s study intention, qualification route, preferences and real information needs. Family context, hobbies or financial background should not become stereotypes that determine academic ability or eligibility; optional collection still needs a clear purpose and student control.

findings.implication: Test optional budget ranges and goals before collecting detailed parent or household records. Ask which detail changes the result, explain why it is requested, and let the student correct or omit it. Separate admission rules from preference-based matching.

No reviewed source establishes this product’s city-level recruitability, typical app budget, paid decision cycle or conversion.

proposedInitialLearningCohort.label: Research-design proposal, not founder-approved restriction or a statistically representative sample
proposedInitialLearningCohort.definition: Indian students reachable through actual founder contacts or explicitly permitted community access, currently considering Germany for a bachelor’s or master’s path and able to describe a recent real planning decision.
proposedInitialLearningCohort.mix: Cover all four degree-level × decision-stage cells. Give master’s questions appropriate attention because the founder emphasizes them, while retaining bachelor interviews; this is not a claim about their national proportions.
proposedInitialLearningCohort.geography: No city ranking. Start where the founder can actually recruit suitable participants; record access and response evidence.
proposedInitialLearningCohort.agePolicy: If no tested guardian flow exists, consider consenting adult volunteers for the first pilot. This requires a founder choice and does not remove bachelor support from the intended product.
requiredForResearch: A current Germany study-planning decision or shortlist
Preferred language and intended intake if known
What sources/workarounds they used and what remains unresolved
proposedInitialLearningCohort.samplingWarning: Purposive discovery, not a basis for population, prevalence or conversion estimates.

gaps: No direct student interviews, observed prototype sessions, app-use habits, abandonment causes or willingness-to-pay evidence are established for this product.
No credible current distribution of the proposed four cells among Indian Germany prospects; enrolled stock and partial application figures do not establish it.
No validated typical age, income, budget, degree field, local city density, buyer influence order, sales cycle or app spend.
The founder’s actual campus/alumni access, current capacity and recruitment permission are still unknown.

Survey findings have distinct samples and questions; the Oxford page identifies two datasets and Acumen explicitly disclaims representativeness. Do not merge their percentages or treat them as Germany subgroup estimates.
The dMAT affected-field list and applicant-specific transition outcome remain unresolved; the supplemental APS freshness check must remain attached to any rule discussion.
The exact purpose and incremental value of optional family, hobby and project details must be learned rather than inferred from founder intent.
redFlags: A vivid persona with invented income, budget, age, city, quote or purchase cycle would create false certainty.
Free initial use and parental education funding do not validate future app payment.
A budget or academic mark alone cannot determine a verified match across both study levels.
Official free personalized guidance already exists; the user’s unmet job must be demonstrated rather than assumed.
yellowFlags: Both degree levels and both stages broaden the evaluation surface; keep the learning matrix explicit while narrowing the first verified data slice.
Family influence does not establish parental account access or consent to share an adult student’s data.
Regional official summaries may lag rule-setting sources. Intake-dependent APS changes must not be hardcoded from an older summary.
Public networks, event pages and digital search interest do not establish cheap or guaranteed recruitment.
summary: Use decision stage and qualification route to organize discovery, not demographic stereotypes. Recruit a purposive mix of real Indian students considering Germany across both degree levels and explorer/checker modes. Treat family roles, trust criteria, optional data value and future payment as things to learn directly.
